name: Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium
assumptions: Stand plan: eight OSM stand ways plus two short blocks either side of the pavilion that OSM omits but the satellite shows.
Terrace rake, 0.42 m per row, 11 lower and 9 upper rows (5 upper on the north and north-east stands): row counts estimated from satellite lines; stand top about 11 m, fitted to the field-side photo.
Pavilion height 20.5 m, scaled from the photo using OSM width; individual level heights are read from photos and approximate.
Pavilion identified as the OSM largest stand on the south side: its plan matches the satellite flat roof and the seating bands.
One press photo with this pavilion is captioned Pindi Club Ground; its architecture matches the stadium photos and it was used for gangway and level counts.
Media Box 17 m, derived from the visible side wall on the satellite; floors and glazing bands are the plainest plausible form.
Six masts: bases read from satellite mast images and shadows, about 60 degrees apart; 44 m lamp height fitted to photo; the head is a single LED panel, the real cluster layout is not visible.
Sponsor panel on each mast is a plain coloured box, no lettering.
Two video screens at stand junctions, read from satellite shadows and white top edges; screen height and frame are estimates.
White strip behind the north and north-east stands treated as a flat band; whether it is canopy or roof is unknown.
No photo of any outer face or entrance was found (three web searches, 9 Nov 2026): rear walls of the stands are plain walls with piers, and no gates are modelled.
Outer face colour of the whole bowl is a guess, taken from the pale stand end walls in RWPCS3; it is not sampled from an outer face.
Pavilion rear wall is plain with no windows, doors or floor bands because none is documented. Its colour is the same guess as the bowl.
On the satellite a dark strip about 3 m wide lies just outside the pavilion's white edge strip; whether it is the wall seen at a lean, a recess or a lean-to is unknown, and it is not modelled.

Pavilion roof: pale inner part, darker outer band 5.5 m wide and white edge strip follow satellite tones and widths, placed against the OSM rear line. The band is modelled level with the roof; any change of level is unknown. The strip is modelled as a coping 1.45 m tall, height a guess.
Pavilion column spacing 3.0 degrees (about 4.7 m at the column line), measured from the field-side photo using the gangways as scale.
Pitch axis bearing 8 estimated from worn strips on the satellite; the sight screens stand in front of pavilion and Media Box as in the photos.
Colours sampled by eye from satellite and photos; 2025 seat colours follow the satellite dark blocks with white star patterns.
Roof hut and flag mast sized from photos. Rear cells behind the south-east stands are plain boxes from the satellite grid; parked vehicles and vegetation are left out.
